title: Rabbi Yosi Ketanta
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Mishnah Sotah, chapter 9, mishnah 15](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Sotah.9.15): when he died, the pious ceased. Why was he called Ketanta? Because he was the “small one” among the pious. In the Gemara there he is called Abba Yosi ben Ketunta. The Yerushalmi reads “Yosi ben Ketunta, who was the epitome of the pious,” and says: “When Rabbi Yosi Hasida and Rabbi Yosi Ketunta died, men of piety ceased.” From this we see that Rabbi Yosi Hasida is not Rabbi Yosi Ketunta; see the entry Isi ben Yehudah.[^1]

notes.text: תמציתן means “epitome.” The Yerushalmi’s Mishnah clause reads תמציתן של חסידים; its later discussion has תמציתן/תמציתו variants. The forms Ketanta, Ketunta and Kitunta are spelling variants. “Small one” renders Hyman’s first explanation literally; the distinction between the two Yosi figures is his inference.
